karten.s0: For $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{n}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2}$: the polynomial $\lambda^2-(a+d)\lambda+(ad-bc)$ factors into $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{(\lambda-\lambda_1)(\lambda-\lambda_2)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lambda^2-(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\lambda+\lambda_1\lambda_2}$. Comparing coefficients gives $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{a+d}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}$ and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{ad-bc}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lambda_1\lambda_2}$.
s: For arbitrary $n$, $p(\lambda)$ likewise factors into $(\lambda_1-\lambda)(\lambda_2-\lambda)\cdots(\lambda_n-\lambda)$; the sign is right because the term $(-\lambda)^n$ occurs in $\det(\mathbf{A}-\lambda\mathbf{I})$. Setting $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lambda}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0}$ gives $\det\mathbf{A}$ on the left and $\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_n$ on the right. For the trace, compare the coefficients of $\lambda^{n-1}$. On the right, they are $(-1)^{n-1}(\lambda_1+\dots+\lambda_n)$. On the left, in the Laplace expansion only the product of the diagonal entries $(a_{11}-\lambda)\cdots(a_{nn}-\lambda)$ yields such a high power of $\lambda$, with the coefficient $(-1)^{n-1}(a_{11}+\dots+a_{nn})$.

For the last statement: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{B})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_i(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{B})_{ii}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_i\sum_la_{il}b_{li}}$ and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{B}\mathbf{A})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_l\sum_ib_{li}a_{il}}$. This is the same double sum, only ordered differently.

karten.v: What does “change of basis” mean?
karten.r: The transition from $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$ is called a change of basis.

karten.v: What does “diagonalizable” mean?
karten.r: A matrix that can be written in this way is called diagonalizable.

karten.v: What does “principal axes” mean?
karten.r: The directions of the eigenvectors are therefore called the principal axes of the quadratic form.

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.3 (Diagonalization)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{S}^{-1}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{S}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n),\qquad\text{so}\qquad \mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\mathbf{S}^{-1} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.4 (Powers and sequences in the eigenbasis)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{x}_k}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{i=1}^nc_i\,\lambda_i^k\,\mathbf s_i\qquad\text{with}\qquad \mathbf{c}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{S}^{-1}\mathbf{x}_0 .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.7 (Spectral theorem)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{Q}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\mathbf{Q}^{\top}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i\,\mathbf{q}_i\mathbf{q}_i^{\top} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.8 (Principal axes of a quadratic form)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lambda_1c_1^2+\lambda_2c_2^2+\dots+\lambda_nc_n^2 .}$$

karten.v: In the ______ of the columns of $\mathbf{S}$, the map $\mathbf{A}$ has the matrix $\mathbf{S}^{-1}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{S}$; eigenvalues, trace and determinant stay the same.
karten.r: In the basis of the columns of $\mathbf{S}$, the map $\mathbf{A}$ has the matrix $\mathbf{S}^{-1}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{S}$; eigenvalues, trace and determinant stay the same.

karten.v: A ______ with $n$ independent eigenvectors is diagonal in their basis: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\mathbf{S}^{-1}}$.
karten.r: A matrix with $n$ independent eigenvectors is diagonal in their basis: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\mathbf{S}^{-1}}$.

karten.v: In the eigenbasis, every power of the ______ becomes powers of the eigenvalues; coupled sequences break down into separate sequences, one per eigenvector.
karten.r: In the eigenbasis, every power of the matrix becomes powers of the eigenvalues; coupled sequences break down into separate sequences, one per eigenvector.

karten.v: A ______ matrix has only real eigenvalues and real eigenvectors.
karten.r: A symmetric matrix has only real eigenvalues and real eigenvectors.

karten.v: For a ______ matrix, eigenvectors for different eigenvalues are perpendicular to each other.
karten.r: For a symmetric matrix, eigenvectors for different eigenvalues are perpendicular to each other.

karten.v: Every ______ matrix is $\mathbf{Q}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\mathbf{Q}^{\top}$: diagonal in a suitably rotated set of axes, a weighted sum of projections onto perpendicular axes.
karten.r: Every symmetric matrix is $\mathbf{Q}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\mathbf{Q}^{\top}$: diagonal in a suitably rotated set of axes, a weighted sum of projections onto perpendicular axes.

karten.v: In the eigenbasis, every ______ becomes the sum $\sum_i\lambda_ic_i^2$ without cross terms; the eigenvectors are the principal axes of its ellipses, and the semi-axes are $1/\sqrt{\lambda_i}$.
karten.r: In the eigenbasis, every quadratic form becomes the sum $\sum_i\lambda_ic_i^2$ without cross terms; the eigenvectors are the principal axes of its ellipses, and the semi-axes are $1/\sqrt{\lambda_i}$.

karten.v: What does “indefinite” mean?
karten.r: If a symmetric matrix has positive and negative eigenvalues, its form is positive in some directions and negative in others: a saddle. Such a matrix is called indefinite.

karten.v: What does “Rayleigh quotient” mean?
karten.r: The quotient in (8.2) is called the Rayleigh quotient.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 8.1 (Positive definite, positive semidefinite)”?
karten.r: $$\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}>0\qquad\text{for all}\ \mathbf{x}\ne\mathbf{0} ,$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 8.5 (Extreme values of a quadratic form)”?
karten.r: $$\lambda_{\min}\le\frac{\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{x}}\le\lambda_{\max} .$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 8.6 (Cholesky decomposition)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf L\mathbf L^{\top} .}$$

karten.v: ______ means: the quadratic form is positive away from the origin, a bowl; positive semidefinite means: nowhere negative.
karten.r: Positive definite means: the quadratic form is positive away from the origin, a bowl; positive semidefinite means: nowhere negative.

karten.v: A ______ matrix is positive definite if and only if all eigenvalues are positive; positive and negative eigenvalues together give a saddle.
karten.r: A symmetric matrix is positive definite if and only if all eigenvalues are positive; positive and negative eigenvalues together give a saddle.

karten.v: A ______ matrix is positive definite if and only if all pivots or all leading principal minors are positive; for $2\times2$ this means $a>0$ and $ac-b^2>0$.
karten.r: A symmetric matrix is positive definite if and only if all pivots or all leading principal minors are positive; for $2\times2$ this means $a>0$ and $ac-b^2>0$.

karten.v: $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$ is always ______, because $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}\rVert^2}$; with independent columns it is positive definite.
karten.r: $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$ is always positive semidefinite, because $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}\rVert^2}$; with independent columns it is positive definite.

karten.v: On the unit circle, a ______ lies between the smallest and the largest eigenvalue, and these extreme values are attained in the eigendirections.
karten.r: On the unit circle, a quadratic form lies between the smallest and the largest eigenvalue, and these extreme values are attained in the eigendirections.

karten.v: Every ______ matrix is $\mathbf L\mathbf L^{\top}$ with a lower triangular matrix $\mathbf L$; the decomposition is completing the square in matrix form.
karten.r: Every positive definite matrix is $\mathbf L\mathbf L^{\top}$ with a lower triangular matrix $\mathbf L$; the decomposition is completing the square in matrix form.

karten.v: What does “right singular vectors” mean?
karten.r: Orthonormal eigenvectors $\mathbf{v}_1,\dots,\mathbf{v}_n$ of $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$ for the eigenvalues $d_1^2,\dots,d_n^2$ are called right singular vectors of $\mathbf{A}$.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 9.1 (Singular values)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{d_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sqrt{\lambda_j},\qquad d_1\ge d_2\ge\dots\ge d_n\ge0 ,}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 9.3 (Singular vectors)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{u}_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}_j}{d_j},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_j\mathbf{u}_j ,}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 9.4 (Singular value decomposition)”?
karten.r:
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{U}\mathbf{D}\mathbf{V}^{\top}}$$
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{j=1}^rd_j\,\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 9.7 (Spectral norm)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\max_{\mathbf{x}\ne\mathbf{0}}\frac{\lVert\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}\rVert}{\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 9.8 (Largest and smallest stretch)”?
karten.r: $$d_n\,\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert\le\lVert\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}\rVert\le d_1\,\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert .$$

karten.v: The ______ of the symmetric matrix $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$ are perpendicular directions whose images under $\mathbf{A}$ are again perpendicular to each other; the images have the lengths $\sqrt{\lambda_i}$.
karten.r: The eigenvectors of the symmetric matrix $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$ are perpendicular directions whose images under $\mathbf{A}$ are again perpendicular to each other; the images have the lengths $\sqrt{\lambda_i}$.

karten.v: The ______ $d_j$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$; they measure how strongly $\mathbf{A}$ stretches in its principal directions, and the number of positive ones is the rank.
karten.r: The singular values $d_j$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$; they measure how strongly $\mathbf{A}$ stretches in its principal directions, and the number of positive ones is the rank.

karten.v: The ______ $\mathbf{v}_j$ are eigenvectors of $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$, the left ones are $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{u}_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}_j/d_j}$; both families are orthonormal, and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_j\mathbf{u}_j}$.
karten.r: The right singular vectors $\mathbf{v}_j$ are eigenvectors of $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A}$, the left ones are $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{u}_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}_j/d_j}$; both families are orthonormal, and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_j\mathbf{u}_j}$.

karten.v: Every ______ is $\mathbf{U}\mathbf{D}\mathbf{V}^{\top}$ with two orthogonal matrices and the singular values on the diagonal of $\mathbf{D}$, or, equivalently, a sum $\sum_jd_j\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}$.
karten.r: Every matrix is $\mathbf{U}\mathbf{D}\mathbf{V}^{\top}$ with two orthogonal matrices and the singular values on the diagonal of $\mathbf{D}$, or, equivalently, a sum $\sum_jd_j\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}$.

karten.v: Every ______ rotates, stretches along the axes and rotates again, up to reflections; the unit circle becomes an ellipse with the semi-axes $d_j\mathbf{u}_j$.
karten.r: Every matrix rotates, stretches along the axes and rotates again, up to reflections; the unit circle becomes an ellipse with the semi-axes $d_j\mathbf{u}_j$.

karten.v: A ______ is the sum of $r$ building blocks $d_j\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}$ of rank $1$; the $\mathbf{u}_j$ with $d_j>0$ span the column space, and the $\mathbf{v}_j$ with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{d_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0}$ span the null space.
karten.r: A matrix is the sum of $r$ building blocks $d_j\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}$ of rank $1$; the $\mathbf{u}_j$ with $d_j>0$ span the column space, and the $\mathbf{v}_j$ with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{d_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0}$ span the null space.

karten.v: For ______ matrices, the singular values are the magnitudes of the eigenvalues, and for positive semidefinite ones the singular value decomposition is the spectral decomposition.
karten.r: For symmetric matrices, the singular values are the magnitudes of the eigenvalues, and for positive semidefinite ones the singular value decomposition is the spectral decomposition.

karten.v: The ______ $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_1}$ is the largest factor by which $\mathbf{A}$ lengthens a vector; the smallest is $d_n$.
karten.r: The spectral norm $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_1}$ is the largest factor by which $\mathbf{A}$ lengthens a vector; the smallest is $d_n$.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 10.1 (Frobenius norm)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_F}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^na_{ij}^2} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 10.2 (Frobenius norm and singular values)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_F^2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_1^2+d_2^2+\dots+d_r^2 .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 10.3 (Truncated singular value decomposition)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}_k}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{j=1}^kd_j\,\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “The truncated decomposition”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{A}_k\rVert_2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_{k+1},\qquad \lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{A}_k\rVert_F}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sqrt{d_{k+1}^2+\dots+d_r^2} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 10.4 (Eckart–Young theorem)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}\rVert_2\ge d_{k+1}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{A}_k\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}\rVert_F\ge\sqrt{d_{k+1}^2+\dots+d_r^2}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{A}_k\rVert_F .}$$

karten.v: The ______ is the Euclidean norm of all entries; its square is the sum of the squared singular values.
karten.r: The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of all entries; its square is the sum of the squared singular values.

karten.v: $\mathbf{A}_k$ keeps the $k$ largest building blocks; the error has the remaining ______, and its spectral norm is $d_{k+1}$.
karten.r: $\mathbf{A}_k$ keeps the $k$ largest building blocks; the error has the remaining singular values, and its spectral norm is $d_{k+1}$.

karten.v: The truncated decomposition $\mathbf{A}_k$ is the best approximation of ______ $k$, in the spectral norm as well as in the Frobenius norm.
karten.r: The truncated decomposition $\mathbf{A}_k$ is the best approximation of rank $k$, in the spectral norm as well as in the Frobenius norm.

karten.v: An image of ______ $k$ needs $k(m+n+1)$ numbers; the truncated decomposition is the best such image, and $\sum_{j\le k}d_j^2/\sum_jd_j^2$ tells how much is preserved.
karten.r: An image of rank $k$ needs $k(m+n+1)$ numbers; the truncated decomposition is the best such image, and $\sum_{j\le k}d_j^2/\sum_jd_j^2$ tells how much is preserved.

karten.v: What does “left inverse” mean?
karten.r: A matrix $\mathbf F\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf F\mathbf{A}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{I}_n}$ is called a left inverse of $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$.

karten.v: What does “right inverse” mean?
karten.r: A matrix $\mathbf G\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf G}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{I}_m}$ is called a right inverse of $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$.

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 11.2 (Left inverse)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf F}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A})^{-1}\mathbf{A}^{\top}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 11.4 (Right inverse and shortest solution)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf G}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^{\top})^{-1}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 11.5 (Pseudoinverse)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}^+}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{V}\mathbf{D}^+\mathbf{U}^{\top}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{j=1}^r\frac1{d_j}\,\mathbf{v}_j\mathbf{u}_j^{\top} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 11.6 (Pseudoinverse and least squares)”?
karten.r: $$\begin{gathered} \mathbf{A}^+=(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A})^{-1}\mathbf{A}^{\top}\quad\text{for independent columns},\\ \mathbf{A}^+=\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^{\top})^{-1}\quad\text{for independent rows}. \end{gathered}$$

karten.v: A ______ with independent columns has the left inverse $(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A})^{-1}\mathbf{A}^{\top}$; it maps $\mathbf{y}$ to the best approximate solution.
karten.r: A matrix with independent columns has the left inverse $(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A})^{-1}\mathbf{A}^{\top}$; it maps $\mathbf{y}$ to the best approximate solution.

karten.v: A ______ with independent rows has the right inverse $\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^{\top})^{-1}$; it delivers the shortest solution.
karten.r: A matrix with independent rows has the right inverse $\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^{\top})^{-1}$; it delivers the shortest solution.

karten.v: The ______ $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}^+}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{V}\mathbf{D}^+\mathbf{U}^{\top}}$ inverts every building block $d_j\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}$ with $d_j>0$ and maps the directions for the singular value $0$ to zero.
karten.r: The pseudoinverse $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{A}^+}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{V}\mathbf{D}^+\mathbf{U}^{\top}}$ inverts every building block $d_j\mathbf{u}_j\mathbf{v}_j^{\top}$ with $d_j>0$ and maps the directions for the singular value $0$ to zero.

karten.v: For every ______, $\mathbf{A}^+\mathbf{y}$ is a best approximate solution, and among several the shortest; with independent columns or rows, $\mathbf{A}^+$ is the left or right inverse.
karten.r: For every matrix, $\mathbf{A}^+\mathbf{y}$ is a best approximate solution, and among several the shortest; with independent columns or rows, $\mathbf{A}^+$ is the left or right inverse.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 12.1 (Condition number)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\kappa(\mathbf{A})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{d_1}{d_n},}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 12.2 (Error amplification)”?
karten.r: $$\frac{\lVert\Delta\mathbf{x}\rVert}{\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert}\le\kappa(\mathbf{A})\,\frac{\lVert\Delta\mathbf{y}\rVert}{\lVert\mathbf{y}\rVert} .$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 12.3 (Distance to the nearest singular matrix)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\min_{\mathbf{B}\ \text{singular}}\frac{\lVert\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{B}\rVert_2}{\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_2}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac1{\kappa(\mathbf{A})} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 12.4 (Condition number of the Gram matrix)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\kappa(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{A})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\kappa(\mathbf{A})^2 .}$$

karten.v: If the lines of a system of equations intersect almost in parallel, small changes in the data shift the ______ a lot.
karten.r: If the lines of a system of equations intersect almost in parallel, small changes in the data shift the solution a lot.

karten.v: The ______ $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\kappa(\mathbf{A})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_1/d_n}$ is the largest factor by which $\mathbf{A}^{-1}$ can enlarge a relative error of the data in the solution.
karten.r: The condition number $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\kappa(\mathbf{A})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{d_1/d_n}$ is the largest factor by which $\mathbf{A}^{-1}$ can enlarge a relative error of the data in the solution.

karten.v: $1/\kappa(\mathbf{A})$ is the relative ______ to the nearest singular matrix; the determinant says nothing about this, because it depends on the size of the matrix.
karten.r: $1/\kappa(\mathbf{A})$ is the relative distance to the nearest singular matrix; the determinant says nothing about this, because it depends on the size of the matrix.

karten.v: The ______ work with $\kappa(\mathbf{A})^2$, the QR decomposition with $\kappa(\mathbf{A})$; well-chosen units lower the condition number.
karten.r: The normal equations work with $\kappa(\mathbf{A})^2$, the QR decomposition with $\kappa(\mathbf{A})$; well-chosen units lower the condition number.

karten.v: What does “secant line” mean?
karten.r: You draw a line through the two points $(x,\,f(x))$ and $(x+h,\,f(x+h))$ of the graph. Such a line through two points of a curve is called a secant line.

karten.v: What does “limit” mean?
karten.r: In general, a quantity that depends on $h$ has the limit $c$ as $h\to0$ if it lies arbitrarily close to $c$ as soon as $h$ is close enough to $0$ and not equal to $0$.

karten.v: What does “differentiable” mean?
karten.r: A function $f$ is called differentiable at the point $x$ if the difference quotient has a limit as $h\to0$.

karten.v: What does “tangent line” mean?
karten.r: The line through $(x,\,f(x))$ with the slope $f'(x)$ is called the tangent line to the graph.

karten.v: What does “kink” mean?
karten.r: A typical exception is a kink: a point at which the graph continues without a jump but has a different slope to its left than to its right.

karten.v: What does “linear approximation” mean?
karten.r: The expression $f(x)+f'(x)\,h$ is called the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $x$, and $r(h)$ is its error.

karten.v: What does “second derivative” mean?
karten.r: If the derivative function $f'$ is differentiable at the point $x$, then $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f''(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{(f')'(x)}$ is called the second derivative of $f$ at the point $x$.

karten.v: What does “curvature” mean?
karten.r: The second derivative therefore measures the curvature of the graph, more precisely: how fast its slope changes.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 1.1 (Difference quotient)”?
karten.r: $$\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 1.2 (Derivative)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 1.3 (Linear approximation)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(x)+f'(x)\,h+r(h)\qquad\text{with}\qquad \lim_{h\to0}\frac{r(h)}{h}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0 .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 1.4 (Differentiation rules)”?
karten.r: $$\begin{aligned} (u+v)'&=u'+v' &&\text{(sum rule)}\\ (c\,u)'&=c\,u' &&\text{(constant multiple rule)}\\ (u\,v)'&=u'\,v+u\,v' &&\text{(product rule)}\\ \Bigl(\frac uv\Bigr)'&=\frac{u'\,v-u\,v'}{v^2}\quad\text{if }v(x)\ne0 &&\text{(quotient rule)} \end{aligned}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 1.6 (Quadratic approximation)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(x)+f'(x)\,h+\tfrac12f''(x)\,h^2+r_2(h)\qquad\text{with}\qquad\lim_{h\to0}\frac{r_2(h)}{h^2}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0 .}$$

karten.v: The ______ is the change in the function value divided by the change in the input, the average slope between two points of the graph.
karten.r: The difference quotient is the change in the function value divided by the change in the input, the average slope between two points of the graph.

karten.v: The ______ $f'(x)$ is the limit of the secant slopes, that is, the slope of the tangent line; at a kink it does not exist.
karten.r: The derivative $f'(x)$ is the limit of the secant slopes, that is, the slope of the tangent line; at a kink it does not exist.

karten.v: Near $x$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(x)+f'(x)\,h}$; the ______ is the factor by which small changes are passed on, and the error vanishes faster than $h$.
karten.r: Near $x$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(x)+f'(x)\,h}$; the derivative is the factor by which small changes are passed on, and the error vanishes faster than $h$.

karten.v: With the basic ______ in the table and the rules for sums, multiples, products and quotients, you differentiate compound formulas without forming a limit.
karten.r: With the basic derivatives in the table and the rules for sums, multiples, products and quotients, you differentiate compound formulas without forming a limit.

karten.v: The ______ measures how fast the slope changes, that is, the curvature; with it, the approximation becomes $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(x)+f'(x)\,h+\tfrac12f''(x)\,h^2}$.
karten.r: The second derivative measures how fast the slope changes, that is, the curvature; with it, the approximation becomes $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(x)+f'(x)\,h+\tfrac12f''(x)\,h^2}$.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 2.1 (Composition)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{(f\circ g)(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f\bigl(g(x)\bigr)}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 2.2 (Chain rule)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{(f\circ g)'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f'\bigl(g(x)\bigr)\cdot g'(x).}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 2.3 (Chain rule for many links)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\mathrm{d} u_L}{\mathrm{d} x}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f_L'(u_{L-1})\cdot f_{L-1}'(u_{L-2})\cdots f_1'(u_0).}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 2.4 (Logistic function)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac1{1+\mathrm{e}^{-x}}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 2.5 (Derivative of the logistic function)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sigma(x)\,\bigl(1-\sigma(x)\bigr).}$$

karten.v: A ______ $f\circ g$ applies first $g$ and then $f$; the order cannot be swapped.
karten.r: A composition $f\circ g$ applies first $g$ and then $f$; the order cannot be swapped.

karten.v: In a ______, the derivatives of the stages multiply, each evaluated at the point where its stage operates: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{(f\circ g)'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f'(g(x))\,g'(x)}$.
karten.r: In a composition, the derivatives of the stages multiply, each evaluated at the point where its stage operates: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{(f\circ g)'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f'(g(x))\,g'(x)}$.

karten.v: In a long chain, the ______ is the product of the derivatives of all links; you first compute the intermediate values, then the factors.
karten.r: In a long chain, the derivative is the product of the derivatives of all links; you first compute the intermediate values, then the factors.

karten.v: The ______ $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})}$ maps every number smoothly into the interval between $0$ and $1$; its derivative is $\sigma(1-\sigma)$, at most $\tfrac14$, and can be computed from the function value alone.
karten.r: The logistic function $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})}$ maps every number smoothly into the interval between $0$ and $1$; its derivative is $\sigma(1-\sigma)$, at most $\tfrac14$, and can be computed from the function value alone.

karten.v: How can “The derivative of the logistic function” be derived?
karten.z:
The following holds:

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sigma(x)\,\bigl(1-\sigma(x)\bigr).}$$
(2.4)

The derivative is positive everywhere and at most $\tfrac14$; it takes its largest value $\tfrac14$ at the point $0$.
karten.s0:
The function is a chain with three links: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{u_1}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{-x}$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{u_2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1+\mathrm{e}^{u_1}}$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1/u_2}$. The factors are $-1$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathrm{e}^{u_1}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathrm{e}^{-x}}$ and $-1/u_2^2$. By (2.2),

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\sigma'(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{-\frac1{(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})^2}\cdot\mathrm{e}^{-x}\cdot(-1)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-x}}{(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})^2}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac1{1+\mathrm{e}^{-x}}\cdot\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-x}}{1+\mathrm{e}^{-x}} .}$$
s: The first factor is $\sigma(x)$. The second is $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})-1}{1+\mathrm{e}^{-x}}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1-\sigma(x)}$. Because $\sigma(x)$ lies between $0$ and $1$, both factors are positive. For a number $p$ between $0$ and $1$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{p\,(1-p)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac14-(p-\tfrac12)^2\le\tfrac14}$, with equality exactly for $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{p}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac12}$, that is, for $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{x}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0}$.

karten.v: What does “function of $d$ variables” mean?
karten.r: A function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ assigns a number $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(x_1,\dots,x_d)}$ to every vector $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^d$; it is called a function of $d$ variables.

karten.v: What does “level set” mean?
karten.r: For a number $c$, the set of all $\mathbf{x}$ with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{c}$ is called the level set of $f$ for the value $c$.

karten.v: What does “contour line” mean?
karten.r: For $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{d}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2}$ it is usually a curve and is then called a contour line.

karten.v: What does “cross-section curve” mean?
karten.r: The cut surface shows a curve as its edge, the cross-section curve, and its slope is the sensitivity you are looking for.

karten.v: What does “tangent plane” mean?
karten.r: Under the magnifying glass, smooth terrain near a point looks like a tilted plate: this is the tangent plane.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 3.2 (Partial derivative)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_j}(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(\mathbf{x}+h\,\mathbf{e}_j)-f(\mathbf{x})}{h},}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 3.3 (Gradient)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\begin{pmatrix}\partial_1f(\mathbf{x})\\ \vdots\\ \partial_df(\mathbf{x})\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^d}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “The linear approximation in space”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(\mathbf{x})+\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{h}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(\mathbf{x})+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jf(\mathbf{x})\,h_j .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 3.4 (Differentiability)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lim_{\mathbf{h}\to\mathbf{0}}\frac{f(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})-f(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{g}^{\top}\mathbf{h}}{\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0 .}$$

karten.v: A function of $d$ variables assigns a number to every ______; with two variables you picture it as a landscape whose contour lines connect locations of equal height.
karten.r: A function of $d$ variables assigns a number to every vector; with two variables you picture it as a landscape whose contour lines connect locations of equal height.

karten.v: The ______ $\partial f/\partial x_j$ is the slope in the direction of the $x_j$-axis: you differentiate with respect to $x_j$ and hold all other variables fixed.
karten.r: The partial derivative $\partial f/\partial x_j$ is the slope in the direction of the $x_j$-axis: you differentiate with respect to $x_j$ and hold all other variables fixed.

karten.v: The ______ is the column vector of all partial derivatives, with the same shape as $\mathbf{x}$.
karten.r: The gradient is the column vector of all partial derivatives, with the same shape as $\mathbf{x}$.

karten.v: ______ means that the linear approximation with the gradient has an error that vanishes faster than $\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert$; continuous partial derivatives guarantee this, their mere existence does not.
karten.r: Differentiable means that the linear approximation with the gradient has an error that vanishes faster than $\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert$; continuous partial derivatives guarantee this, their mere existence does not.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 4.1 (Directional derivative)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_{\mathbf{u}}f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\lim_{t\to0}\frac{f(\mathbf{x}+t\,\mathbf{u})-f(\mathbf{x})}{t}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 4.2 (Directional derivative and gradient)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_{\mathbf{u}}f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{u} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 4.3 (Steepest ascent)”?
karten.r: $$-\lVert\nabla f(\mathbf{x})\rVert\le D_{\mathbf{u}}f(\mathbf{x})\le\lVert\nabla f(\mathbf{x})\rVert .$$

karten.v: The slope in the direction of a ______ $\mathbf{u}$ is the dot product $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{u}$.
karten.r: The slope in the direction of a unit vector $\mathbf{u}$ is the dot product $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{u}$.

karten.v: The ______ points in the direction of steepest ascent, and its length is the slope there; against the gradient, the path leads downhill most steeply.
karten.r: The gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent, and its length is the slope there; against the gradient, the path leads downhill most steeply.

karten.v: Along a ______, $f$ does not change; that is why the gradient is perpendicular to it.
karten.r: Along a contour line, $f$ does not change; that is why the gradient is perpendicular to it.

karten.v: The negative ______ points downhill most steeply, but it points at the lowest point only for round contour lines; for elongated contour lines it points past it.
karten.r: The negative gradient points downhill most steeply, but it points at the lowest point only for round contour lines; for elongated contour lines it points past it.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 5.1 (Vector-valued function)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\begin{pmatrix}g_1(\mathbf{x})\\ \vdots\\ g_m(\mathbf{x})\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^m}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 5.2 (Jacobian matrix)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\begin{pmatrix}\dfrac{\partial g_1}{\partial x_1}&\cdots&\dfrac{\partial g_1}{\partial x_n}\\ \vdots&&\vdots\\ \dfrac{\partial g_m}{\partial x_1}&\cdots&\dfrac{\partial g_m}{\partial x_n}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \bigl(\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})\bigr)_{ij}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{\partial g_i}{\partial x_j}(\mathbf{x}),}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 5.3 (Linear approximation of a vector-valued function)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})+\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{h}+\mathbf{r}(\mathbf{h})\qquad\text{with}\qquad\lim_{\mathbf{h}\to\mathbf{0}}\frac{\lVert\mathbf{r}(\mathbf{h})\rVert}{\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0 .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 5.4 (Jacobian matrices of the building blocks)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\varphi'(x_1),\,\dots,\,\varphi'(x_n)\bigr).}$$

karten.v: A ______ function $\mathbf{g}:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ consists of $m$ functions of $n$ variables, one for each output.
karten.r: A vector-valued function $\mathbf{g}:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ consists of $m$ functions of $n$ variables, one for each output.

karten.v: The ______ has one row per output and one column per input; its entry $(i,j)$ is $\partial g_i/\partial x_j$.
karten.r: The Jacobian matrix has one row per output and one column per input; its entry $(i,j)$ is $\partial g_i/\partial x_j$.

karten.v: Near $\mathbf{x}$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})+\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{h}}$; the ______ is the matrix of the linear map that $\mathbf{g}$ acts like on a small scale.
karten.r: Near $\mathbf{x}$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})+\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{h}}$; the Jacobian matrix is the matrix of the linear map that $\mathbf{g}$ acts like on a small scale.

karten.v: The ______ of $\mathbf{x}\mapsto\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}$ is $\mathbf{A}$; that of an elementwise function is the diagonal matrix of the individual derivatives.
karten.r: The Jacobian matrix of $\mathbf{x}\mapsto\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}$ is $\mathbf{A}$; that of an elementwise function is the diagonal matrix of the individual derivatives.

karten.v: What does “curve” mean?
karten.r: A curve is a function $\boldsymbol{\gamma}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^d$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{t\mapsto\boldsymbol{\gamma}(t)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{(\gamma_1(t),\dots,\gamma_d(t))^{\top}}$.

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 6.1 (Chain rule for several variables)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf f\circ\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf f}\bigl(\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})\bigr)\,\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x}).}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Sum over all paths”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\partial F}{\partial x_j}(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{\partial f}{\partial u_i}(\mathbf{u})\,\frac{\partial u_i}{\partial x_j}(\mathbf{x}),\qquad \mathbf{u}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}).}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 6.2 (Gradient of a composition)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla(f\circ\mathbf{g})(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\,\nabla f(\mathbf{u}).}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Derivative along a curve”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t}f\bigl(\boldsymbol{\gamma}(t)\bigr)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\nabla f\bigl(\boldsymbol{\gamma}(t)\bigr)^{\top}\boldsymbol{\gamma}'(t).}$$

karten.v: The ______ of a composition is the product of the Jacobian matrices of the stages, with the stage applied last on the left: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf f\circ\mathbf{g}}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf f}\,\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}}$.
karten.r: The Jacobian matrix of a composition is the product of the Jacobian matrices of the stages, with the stage applied last on the left: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf f\circ\mathbf{g}}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf f}\,\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}}$.

karten.v: Componentwise, the chain rule is a sum over all paths from the input to the output; along each path, the ______ are multiplied.
karten.r: Componentwise, the chain rule is a sum over all paths from the input to the output; along each path, the local derivatives are multiplied.

karten.v: The ______ of a composition is the transposed Jacobian matrix of the inner function times the gradient of the outer one: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla(f\circ\mathbf{g})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}^{\top}\nabla f}$.
karten.r: The gradient of a composition is the transposed Jacobian matrix of the inner function times the gradient of the outer one: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla(f\circ\mathbf{g})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{J}_{\mathbf{g}}^{\top}\nabla f}$.

karten.v: Along a ______, $f$ changes at the rate $\nabla f^{\top}\boldsymbol{\gamma}'$; within a contour line, this rate is zero.
karten.r: Along a curve, $f$ changes at the rate $\nabla f^{\top}\boldsymbol{\gamma}'$; within a contour line, this rate is zero.

karten.v: What does “layout convention” mean?
karten.r: Such a decision is called a layout convention.

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.2 (Gradients of linear functions)”?
karten.r: $$ extcolor{#1b7f4a}{ abla_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{a}^{ op}\mathbf{x})} extcolor{#15633a}{=} extcolor{#c2410c}{ abla_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}^{ op}\mathbf{a})} extcolor{#15633a}{=} extcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{a},\qquad abla_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y}^{ op}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x})} extcolor{#15633a}{=} extcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}^{ op}\mathbf{y} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.3 (Gradient of a quadratic form)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{A}^{\top})\,\mathbf{x} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.4 (Gradient of the sum of squares)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{-2\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}).}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Differentiating with respect to a matrix”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf E)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(\mathbf{A})+\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\bigl(\nabla_{\mathbf{A}}f\bigr)_{ij}\,e_{ij}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.5 (Two derivatives with respect to a matrix)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\nabla_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{u}\mathbf{v}^{\top},\qquad \nabla_{\mathbf{A}}\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_F^2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2\mathbf{A} .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 7.6 (Backward rule of the matrix product)”?
karten.r: $$ extcolor{#1b7f4a}{ abla_{\mathbf{A}}F} extcolor{#15633a}{=} extcolor{#c2410c}{ abla f(\mathbf{y})\,\mathbf{x}^{ op},\qquad abla_{\mathbf{x}}F} extcolor{#15633a}{=} extcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}^{ op}\, abla f(\mathbf{y}).}$$

karten.v: In this chapter, a ______ has the shape of its variable, and a Jacobian matrix has one row per output; from this follow $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_f}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\nabla f^{\top}}$ and the transpose in the chain rule for gradients.
karten.r: In this chapter, a gradient has the shape of its variable, and a Jacobian matrix has one row per output; from this follow $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{J}_f}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\nabla f^{\top}}$ and the transpose in the chain rule for gradients.

karten.v: The ______ of $\mathbf{a}^{\top}\mathbf{x}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ is $\mathbf{a}$; that of $\mathbf{y}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ is $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{y}$.
karten.r: The gradient of $\mathbf{a}^{\top}\mathbf{x}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ is $\mathbf{a}$; that of $\mathbf{y}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ is $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{y}$.

karten.v: The ______ of $\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ is $(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{A}^{\top})\mathbf{x}$, so $2\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ for symmetric $\mathbf{A}$, and that of $\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert^2$ is $2\mathbf{x}$.
karten.r: The gradient of $\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ is $(\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{A}^{\top})\mathbf{x}$, so $2\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ for symmetric $\mathbf{A}$, and that of $\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert^2$ is $2\mathbf{x}$.

karten.v: The ______ of $\lVert\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}\rVert^2$ is $-2\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x})$; it vanishes exactly where the residual is perpendicular to the columns of $\mathbf{A}$.
karten.r: The gradient of $\lVert\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}\rVert^2$ is $-2\mathbf{A}^{\top}(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x})$; it vanishes exactly where the residual is perpendicular to the columns of $\mathbf{A}$.

karten.v: The ______ of a number with respect to a matrix has the shape of the matrix; for $\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}$ it is the outer product $\mathbf{u}\mathbf{v}^{\top}$, for $\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_F^2$ it is $2\mathbf{A}$.
karten.r: The derivative of a number with respect to a matrix has the shape of the matrix; for $\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}$ it is the outer product $\mathbf{u}\mathbf{v}^{\top}$, for $\lVert\mathbf{A}\rVert_F^2$ it is $2\mathbf{A}$.

karten.v: Backward through $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{y}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}}$: the ______ with respect to $\mathbf{A}$ is $\nabla f(\mathbf{y})\,\mathbf{x}^{\top}$, the one with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ is $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\nabla f(\mathbf{y})$.
karten.r: Backward through $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{y}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}}$: the gradient with respect to $\mathbf{A}$ is $\nabla f(\mathbf{y})\,\mathbf{x}^{\top}$, the one with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ is $\mathbf{A}^{\top}\nabla f(\mathbf{y})$.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 8.1 (Second partial derivatives)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}\Bigl(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_j}\Bigr),}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 8.2 (Hessian matrix)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\begin{pmatrix}\dfrac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_1^2}&\cdots&\dfrac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_1\,\partial x_d}\\ \vdots&&\vdots\\ \dfrac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_d\,\partial x_1}&\cdots&\dfrac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_d^2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \bigl(\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\bigr)_{ij}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}(\mathbf{x}),}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 8.3 (Schwarz's theorem)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_j\,\partial x_i}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 8.4 (Quadratic approximation)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(\mathbf{x})+\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{h}+\tfrac12\,\mathbf{h}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{h}+r_2(\mathbf{h})\qquad\text{with}\qquad\lim_{\mathbf{h}\to\mathbf{0}}\frac{r_2(\mathbf{h})}{\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert^2}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0 .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 8.5 (Curvature in a direction)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\frac{\mathrm{d}^2}{\mathrm{d} t^2}f(\mathbf{x}+t\,\mathbf{u})\Big|_{t=0}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{u}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 8.6 (Curvature and eigenvalues)”?
karten.r: $$\lambda_{\min}\le\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{u}\le\lambda_{\max}.$$

karten.v: ______ differentiate a partial derivative partially once more; the mixed ones describe how the slope in one direction changes as you walk in another direction.
karten.r: Second partial derivatives differentiate a partial derivative partially once more; the mixed ones describe how the slope in one direction changes as you walk in another direction.

karten.v: The ______ collects all second partial derivatives; for a quadratic function $\tfrac12\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}^{\top}\mathbf{x}+c$ it is $\mathbf{A}$ everywhere.
karten.r: The Hessian matrix collects all second partial derivatives; for a quadratic function $\tfrac12\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{b}^{\top}\mathbf{x}+c$ it is $\mathbf{A}$ everywhere.

karten.v: With continuous ______, the order of differentiation does not matter, and the Hessian matrix is symmetric.
karten.r: With continuous second derivatives, the order of differentiation does not matter, and the Hessian matrix is symmetric.

karten.v: Near $\mathbf{x}$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(\mathbf{x})+\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{h}+\tfrac12\mathbf{h}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{h}}$: a plane plus a ______.
karten.r: Near $\mathbf{x}$, $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(\mathbf{x})+\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{h}+\tfrac12\mathbf{h}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{h}}$: a plane plus a quadratic form.

karten.v: The ______ in the direction $\mathbf{u}$ is $\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f\mathbf{u}$; it lies between the smallest and the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian matrix, and their signs decide whether the terrain curves like a bowl or like a saddle.
karten.r: The curvature in the direction $\mathbf{u}$ is $\mathbf{u}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f\mathbf{u}$; it lies between the smallest and the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian matrix, and their signs decide whether the terrain curves like a bowl or like a saddle.

karten.v: How can “The quadratic approximation along a line” be derived?
karten.z:
If $f$ has continuous second partial derivatives near $\mathbf{x}$, then

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{h})}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(\mathbf{x})+\nabla f(\mathbf{x})^{\top}\mathbf{h}+\tfrac12\,\mathbf{h}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{h}+r_2(\mathbf{h})}$$
$$\text{with}$$
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\lim_{\mathbf{h}\to\mathbf{0}}\frac{r_2(\mathbf{h})}{\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert^2}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0 .}$$
(8.4)
karten.s0:
Restrict $f$ to the line through $\mathbf{x}$ in the direction $\mathbf{h}$: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\phi(t)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{f(\mathbf{x}+t\,\mathbf{h})}$. This is a function of one variable. By (6.4), $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\phi'(t)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\nabla f(\mathbf{x}+t\mathbf{h})^{\top}\mathbf{h}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_jh_j\,\partial_jf(\mathbf{x}+t\mathbf{h})}$. You differentiate each term once more with (6.4), this time for the function $\partial_jf$:

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\phi''(t)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{j=1}^dh_j\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}(\mathbf{x}+t\mathbf{h})\,h_i}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\mathbf{h}^{\top}\mathbf{H}_f(\mathbf{x}+t\mathbf{h})\,\mathbf{h} .}$$
s: The quadratic approximation (1.6) of $\phi$ at the point $0$, evaluated at $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{t}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1}$, reads $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\phi(1)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\phi(0)+\phi'(0)+\tfrac12\phi''(0)}$, and that is (8.4). That the error vanishes faster than $\lVert\mathbf{h}\rVert^2$ follows from the continuity of the second derivatives.

karten.v: What does “computational graph” mean?
karten.r: A computational graph consists of nodes and directed edges, that is, arrows between nodes.

karten.v: What does “forward evaluation” mean?
karten.r: The forward evaluation of a computational graph computes all nodes in an order in which each node comes after its predecessors, and it stores every value.

karten.v: What does “local derivative” mean?
karten.r: For an edge from $a$ to $b$, the partial derivative $\partial b/\partial a$ of the elementary operation that computes $b$, taken with respect to its input $a$, is called the local derivative of the edge.

karten.v: Written-out ______ formulas quickly become much longer than the function; with intermediate results stored as numbers, the cost per step stays small.
karten.r: Written-out derivative formulas quickly become much longer than the function; with intermediate results stored as numbers, the cost per step stays small.

karten.v: A ______ breaks a calculation down into elementary operations; its edges show which value enters which other one, and because it is acyclic, there is always an order in which you can evaluate it.
karten.r: A computational graph breaks a calculation down into elementary operations; its edges show which value enters which other one, and because it is acyclic, there is always an order in which you can evaluate it.

karten.v: The ______ evaluates the graph node by node and stores every intermediate value.
karten.r: The forward evaluation evaluates the graph node by node and stores every intermediate value.

karten.v: Each edge carries the ______ of its elementary operation, evaluated with the stored values; the derivative of the result is the sum, over all paths, of the products of these numbers.
karten.r: Each edge carries the local derivative of its elementary operation, evaluated with the stored values; the derivative of the result is the sum, over all paths, of the products of these numbers.

karten.v: What does “adjoint” mean?
karten.r: The adjoint of a node $a$ is $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\bar a}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\partial f/\partial a}$, the derivative of the result with respect to this node when you regard it as an input of the rest of the calculation.

karten.v: What does “reverse mode” mean?
karten.r: In reverse mode, you first carry out the forward evaluation and store all values.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 10.2 (Forward mode)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\dot b}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{a\text{ predecessor of }b}\frac{\partial b}{\partial a}\,\dot a ,}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 10.3 (Reverse mode)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\bar a}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{b\text{ successor of }a}\bar b\,\frac{\partial b}{\partial a}.}$$

karten.v: ______ applies the chain rule with numbers to the computational graph; it is exact up to rounding and needs no formula.
karten.r: Automatic differentiation applies the chain rule with numbers to the computational graph; it is exact up to rounding and needs no formula.

karten.v: ______ carries a tangent value along with every value; one pass yields the derivative in one direction, that is, one column of the Jacobian matrix.
karten.r: Forward mode carries a tangent value along with every value; one pass yields the derivative in one direction, that is, one column of the Jacobian matrix.

karten.v: ______ first calculates forward and stores all values, then calculates the adjoints $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\bar a}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum\bar b\,\partial b/\partial a}$ backward; one backward pass yields the whole gradient.
karten.r: Reverse mode first calculates forward and stores all values, then calculates the adjoints $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\bar a}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum\bar b\,\partial b/\partial a}$ backward; one backward pass yields the whole gradient.

karten.v: ______ delivers all $n$ partial derivatives of a number for a small fixed multiple of one evaluation, independent of $n$; it pays for this with the memory for all intermediate values.
karten.r: Reverse mode delivers all $n$ partial derivatives of a number for a small fixed multiple of one evaluation, independent of $n$; it pays for this with the memory for all intermediate values.

karten.v: ______ multiplies the chain of Jacobian matrices from the left with a row, forward mode from the right with a column; the Jacobian matrices themselves are never formed.
karten.r: Reverse mode multiplies the chain of Jacobian matrices from the left with a row, forward mode from the right with a column; the Jacobian matrices themselves are never formed.

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 11.1 (Forward difference)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_+f(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “The forward difference”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_+f(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f'(x)+\tfrac12f''(x)\,h .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 11.2 (Central difference)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_0f(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 11.3 (Truncation error of the central difference)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_0f(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f'(x)+\tfrac16f'''(x)\,h^2 .}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Theorem 11.4 (Total error of the difference quotients)”?
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{E_+(h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac12|f''(x)|\,h+\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f(x)|}{h}\qquad\text{and}\qquad E_0(h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac16|f'''(x)|\,h^2+\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f(x)|}{2h}}$$

karten.v: What is the formula “Definition 11.5 (Gradient check)”?
karten.r:
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{g_{\mathrm n,j}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{f(\mathbf{x}+h\,\mathbf{e}_j)-f(\mathbf{x}-h\,\mathbf{e}_j)}{2h}.}$$
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\rho_j}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{|g_{\mathrm a,j}-g_{\mathrm n,j}|}{\max\bigl(|g_{\mathrm a,j}|,\,|g_{\mathrm n,j}|\bigr)},}$$

karten.v: The ______ has a truncation error of about $\tfrac12f''(x)\,h$, proportional to the step size.
karten.r: The forward difference has a truncation error of about $\tfrac12f''(x)\,h$, proportional to the step size.

karten.v: The ______ has a truncation error of about $\tfrac16f'''(x)\,h^2$, because the curvature term cancels.
karten.r: The central difference has a truncation error of about $\tfrac16f'''(x)\,h^2$, because the curvature term cancels.

karten.v: Too large an $h$ gives ______, too small a one gives rounding errors; the best choice is $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{h}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{10^{-8}}$ for the forward difference and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{h}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{10^{-5}}$ to $10^{-6}$ for the central one, and the central difference then reaches about eleven instead of eight correct digits.
karten.r: Too large an $h$ gives truncation errors, too small a one gives rounding errors; the best choice is $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{h}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{10^{-8}}$ for the forward difference and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{h}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{10^{-5}}$ to $10^{-6}$ for the central one, and the central difference then reaches about eleven instead of eight correct digits.

karten.v: The ______ compares a computed gradient componentwise with central differences; relative errors above $10^{-2}$ indicate a mistake in the formula, those below $10^{-7}$ a correct formula.
karten.r: The gradient check compares a computed gradient componentwise with central differences; relative errors above $10^{-2}$ indicate a mistake in the formula, those below $10^{-7}$ a correct formula.

karten.v: ______, single precision, too small step sizes and gradients close to zero distort the check; you check at several irregular points.
karten.r: Kinks, single precision, too small step sizes and gradients close to zero distort the check; you check at several irregular points.

karten.v: How can “Why the curvature cancels” be derived?
karten.z:
If $f$ has a continuous third derivative, then

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{D_0f(x)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f'(x)+\tfrac16f'''(x)\,h^2 .}$$
(11.4)

So the truncation error is roughly proportional to $h^2$.
karten.s0:
You continue the quadratic approximation from Section 1.5 by one term. If, as with the parabola there, you also match the third derivative, the term $\tfrac16f'''(x)\,h^3$ is added; the factor $\tfrac16$ arises because the third derivative of $h^3$ equals $6$. Thus

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x\pm h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ f(x)\pm f'(x)\,h+\tfrac12f''(x)\,h^2\pm\tfrac16f'''(x)\,h^3 .}$$
s: If you subtract the two equations from each other, the terms with even powers of $h$ drop out, because they have the same sign in both equations: $f(x)$ and the curvature term $\tfrac12f''h^2$. What remains is $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2f'(x)\,h+\tfrac13f'''(x)\,h^3}$, and dividing by $2h$ gives (11.4). Intuitively: the curvature makes the right secant line steeper and the left one flatter, and the central difference is the mean of the two.

karten.v: How can “The best step size” be derived?
karten.z:
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{E_+(h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac12|f''(x)|\,h+\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f(x)|}{h}}$$
$$\text{and}$$
$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{E_0(h)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac16|f'''(x)|\,h^2+\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f(x)|}{2h}}$$
(11.5)
karten.s0: The numerator contains two function values, each with a rounding error of up to $\tfrac12\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f|$, together up to $\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f|$.
s: For the forward difference, this is divided by $h$, for the central one by $2h$.
On top of that come the truncation errors (11.2) and (11.4).

A function of the form $a\,h+b/h$ with $a,b>0$ has the derivative $a-b/h^2$, which becomes zero at $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{h}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sqrt{b/a}}$; there, the value is $2\sqrt{ab}$.

With $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{a}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac12|f''|}$ and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{b}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f|}$, this gives $h_+$.

For $a\,h^2+b/h$, the derivative is $2ah-b/h^2$, which becomes zero at $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{h^3}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{b/(2a)}$; with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{a}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac16|f'''|}$ and $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{b}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\tfrac12\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}|f|}$, this gives $h_0$.
